title: Secret resume-phase setter live-breakpoint retry (2026-07-16, arm-before-RUN fix applied; still rejected, new failure mode)
purpose: Retry the line-358 BUILD-QUEUE.md two-stage setter replay after fixing the breakpoint-arming sequencing bug documented in secret-combat-resume-setter-breakpoint-attempt-20260716.json (BP/BPDEL typed while the CPU was already free-running). This run's specific fix: arm 'BP 4465:0000' while the debugger console is in a confirmed-stopped state, immediately BEFORE the cursor loop's own first RUN, and require a BPLIST readback to prove registration before proceeding -- never type BP/BPDEL after a RUN has already been issued.

fix_applied.change_summary: Removed the old 'Send-DebuggerKey F5' + 'BPDEL *' + 'BP 4465:0000' + 'RUN' sequence that ran AFTER the cursor loop (which could leave the CPU already free-running through 2D tactical combat). Added an early arm block (lines ~262-276) right after the operand-parser breakpoint hit is confirmed (a genuinely-stopped state), before the cursor loop's for-loop begins: 'BP 4465:0000' then 'BPLIST' with a readback that requires the listing to contain 'BP 4465:0000' and NOT '(Running)', throwing otherwise. The later outcome-control block (lines ~396-419) no longer types BP/BPDEL; it only issues 'RUN' if a snapshot-only poll shows the debugger is NOT already running (Path A), and otherwise leaves the already-free-running CPU untouched (Path B), logging '[secret-resume] debugger already free-running into combat; resume breakpoint stays armed from before RUN'. The stage-2 setter breakpoint (segment:0561) arm also now gets an explicit BPLIST readback+verification before its own RUN.

arm_before_run_proof.claim: This is the one thing this retry set out to prove, and it is now live-verified, not inferred: the resume-phase breakpoint was registered while the debugger was genuinely stopped, before the cursor loop's first RUN, and BPLIST proves it stayed registered.

arm_before_run_proof.breakpoint_never_deleted_before_resume_w: No 'BPDEL' command was sent between this arm and the end of the run (verified by reading tools/trace_secret_begin_selector.ps1's control flow: Path B in the outcome-control block explicitly skips issuing any debugger command at all, per the '[secret-resume] debugger already free-running into combat' log line captured in this run's own stdout).

new_failure_mode.observed: CS=4465 EIP=00000000 was still never seen live in any poll, even though the breakpoint was proven armed and never removed. The debugger console's last live-halt scrollback throughout the entire combat-outcome window remained the stale text from the earlier 411B:0000 cursor-loop hit; every poll during and after tactical combat showed '(Running)' as the live status line, meaning the CPU genuinely never stopped again for the rest of the run.
new_failure_mode.distinguishing_fact: This rules out the previous run's root-cause hypothesis (registration timing/dropped console input) for THIS run: registration is now proven contemporaneously (BPLIST, not post-hoc), and the breakpoint demonstrably stayed armed and unremoved through the entire window. The failure is therefore NOT that the breakpoint failed to register -- it registered and stayed registered -- but that CS:IP apparently never equals 4465:0000 during this route's actual resume execution.
new_failure_mode.loop_exit_cause: The outer combat-outcome while loop exited via 'if ($agentProcess.HasExited) { break }' at approximately 2026-07-16T10:51:50 local, roughly 4 minutes after tactical combat began (2026-07-16T10:47:58) -- far short of the 900-second AutoCombatTimeoutSeconds deadline. The script then threw its own guard: 'bounded Ollama/Quick combat did not return to ECL resume 0x82BC' (tools/trace_secret_begin_selector.ps1:557, captured in build/dosbox-x-secret-combat-resume-setter-20260716-r2.runner.stderr.log).

natural_route_completed_anyway.note: Post-hoc inspection of the final RAM snapshot (captured only because the loop gave up, per the auto-combat-timeout fallback path) again proves the underlying game logic completed the entire resume sequence correctly and natively -- for the second attempt in a row -- while the live breakpoint instrumentation still failed to observe it.

This independently reproduces that the underlying route and address resolution (Area1 word 0x4CCD -> ES:54DC:039A -> physical 0x5515A) are stable and correct across three separate runs (2026-07-15 natural, 2026-07-16 r1, 2026-07-16 r2) -- only the LIVE breakpoint capture at the assumed entry offset 4465:0000 remains unproven.

revised_root_cause_hypothesis.claim_boundary: hypothesis only, not proven this session -- offered to focus the next attempt
revised_root_cause_hypothesis.text: tools/map_secret_runtime_setter.py derives segment 4465 by scanning retained RAM snapshots for the byte-identical setter FUNCTION (prologue at +0x0507, mov es:[di+6A00],dx at +0x0561) and reporting the paragraph-aligned segment that contains it -- by analogy with how segments 411B (parser) and 41B7 (tactical) were derived and separately LIVE-confirmed (both were hit repeatedly, live, at their own offset 0000 during ordinary ECL stepping). Segment 4465's offset-0000 entry, in contrast, has never been LIVE-confirmed in any of the three runs to date -- it is inferred purely by analogy with the other two phases, which is not the same evidentiary strength as a live CS:IP hit. It remains true that the identical ~9KB overlay blob (the ECL VM interpreter code, including its own dispatch-loop head at offset 0000 and the vm_SetMemoryValue-equivalent function at +0x0507/+0x0561) is resident at segment 4465. What is NOT proven is that the resume phase's control flow re-enters that blob via its own offset-0000 head the same way the parser and tactical phases do -- it may instead call directly into a different internal entry point (e.g. straight into the +0x0507 function, or some other offset), skipping offset 0000 entirely for a resume-only call path.
revised_root_cause_hypothesis.falsified_this_session: The previous 'registration timing / dropped console input' hypothesis is now falsified for a run where registration was proven live and contemporaneous. It should not be reused as the explanation for a live-capture failure on 4465:0000 going forward.
revised_root_cause_hypothesis.supported_this_session: Two independent live+post-hoc runs (r1, r2) now agree: 4465 is a real segment containing byte-exact setter bytes, and the natural route completes correctly through it functionally, but its own offset 0000 is never observed live via CS:IP -- consistent with resume entering that blob at an offset other than 0000.

suggested_next_attempt: Stop trying to catch the assumed dispatch-loop re-entry at 4465:0000. Instead arm the write site directly: since the setter function's exact bytes (prologue +0x0507, write +0x0561) are already independently byte-matched in TWO runs' post-hoc RAM, arm 'BP 4465:0561' (or a small set of plausible aligned-segment candidates around it) as the PRIMARY breakpoint for the outcome-control phase, skipping the offset-0000 assumption.

If a direct segment:0561 arm still never fires, the paragraph-aligned segment value itself may be wrong for the LIVE call path (even though it is correct for the RAM byte scan). Consider a broader sweep: arm BP on every 0x10-aligned candidate segment within the known VROOMM overlay-swap arena (see research/pool-runtime-route-overlay-trace.md and research/secret-runtime-setter-relocation.json for the arena's known bounds) at offset 0x0561, one attempt at a time, rather than assuming 4465 specifically for the CALL target (only for the RAM-resident COPY).

Alternatively, single-step (T-flag / F11) forward from the last confirmed-live breakpoint before resume (the combat-gate Enter or the injected-victory Enter) with a bounded step budget, logging CS:IP on every step, to directly observe which segment:offset pair the CPU actually uses to re-enter ECL VM code after tactical combat -- this replaces the analogy-based segment guess with a ground-truth trace, at the cost of a much larger step-count budget and log volume.
Keep the arm-before-RUN + BPLIST-readback discipline from this fix for any of the above -- it is proven correct and should not be regressed.
checkbox_status: BUILD-QUEUE.md line ~358 remains unchecked; this is a second rejected attempt, with the originally-diagnosed breakpoint-arming-timing bug now fixed and proven, but a new, more specific failure mode (live CS:IP never observed at segment 4465 offset 0000, despite proven-armed registration) blocking the live single-step/register capture the acceptance criteria requires.
